items.question: Bioavailability of an intravenous drug is?
items.explanation: IV drugs enter circulation directly, so bioavailability is 100% by definition. Oral drugs are less due to first-pass metabolism.

items.question: Drug showing high first-pass metabolism among these?
items.explanation: Propranolol, lignocaine, GTN, morphine and verapamil undergo extensive first-pass hepatic metabolism.

items.question: Which drug is an SGLT2 inhibitor approved for heart failure even without diabetes?
items.explanation: Dapagliflozin and empagliflozin reduce heart failure hospitalisation and renal decline independent of diabetes status.

items.question: Which route avoids first-pass metabolism?
items.explanation: Sublingual absorption drains into systemic veins, bypassing hepatic first-pass metabolism (e.g. GTN).

items.explanation: Phase I trials (20-100 healthy volunteers) assess safety, tolerability, PK and maximum tolerated dose.

*PharmaCraft Daily - 04 Oct 2026*

🎓 *MBBS* (General Pharmacology)
Q: Bioavailability of an intravenous drug is?
Ans: 100%
Why: IV drugs enter circulation directly, so bioavailability is 100% by definition. Oral drugs are less due to first-pass metabolism.

🩺 *NEET PG* (General Pharmacology)
Q: Drug showing high first-pass metabolism among these?
Ans: Propranolol
Why: Propranolol, lignocaine, GTN, morphine and verapamil undergo extensive first-pass hepatic metabolism.

🏥 *INI-CET* (Recent Advances)
Q: Which drug is an SGLT2 inhibitor approved for heart failure even without diabetes?
Ans: Dapagliflozin
Why: Dapagliflozin and empagliflozin reduce heart failure hospitalisation and renal decline independent of diabetes status.

🌍 *FMGE* (General Pharmacology)
Q: Which route avoids first-pass metabolism?
Ans: Sublingual
Why: Sublingual absorption drains into systemic veins, bypassing hepatic first-pass metabolism (e.g. GTN).

🔬 *MD Pharmacology* (Clinical Trials)
Q: The primary aim of a Phase I trial is to assess?
Ans: Safety and pharmacokinetics
Why: Phase I trials (20-100 healthy volunteers) assess safety, tolerability, PK and maximum tolerated dose.
